rulebook.title: IJF Sport and Organisation Rules (SOR) and IJF Refereeing Rules
rulebook.text_used: judogi, tatami and penalty sections from a secondary summary of the IJF rules read this session (ijf.org itself was not reachable); scores and penalty levels from general knowledge. The IJF revises the refereeing rules every Olympic cycle, so check penalty levels (shido or hansoku-make) against the current edition.

tatami_m.note: contest area and safety area in different colours

scene.text: One athlete in a white judogi, the other in a blue judogi; the jacket covers the thighs and closes left over right, sleeves reach the wrist, trousers reach the ankle; belt tied with a square knot; women wear a plain white T-shirt under the jacket, men nothing under it.
No rings, watches, piercings or other hard objects; long hair tied back; nails cut short; barefoot on the tatami.
Square contest area 8-10 m across inside a 3 m safety area of a different colour; coach chairs at the corners.
One referee on the mat; two judges at the table with the video replay (CARE) system; the referee raises one arm straight up for ippon.

fouls.title: Grabbing the legs
fouls.text: Attacking or blocking with one or both hands or arms below the belt (grabbing the legs or trousers) is penalised.
fouls.legal: tori's hands are on the jacket and sleeves, away from uke's legs

fouls.title: Head diving
fouls.text: Diving head first into the tatami while throwing, bending forward and down, is hansoku-make; tori's head stays up off the mat.
fouls.legal: tori's head is well above the mat

fouls.title: Non-standard grips
fouls.text: A cross grip, a one-sided grip, a belt grip or a grip on the back must be followed by an attack within a few seconds; fingers inside the opponent's sleeve or trouser leg, and the pistol grip on the sleeve end, are penalised.

fouls.title: Hand on the face
fouls.text: Putting a hand, arm, foot or leg directly on the opponent's face is penalised.
fouls.legal: no hand on the opponent's face

fouls.title: Defensive posture
fouls.text: Bending over excessively to avoid being thrown, or holding without attacking, is penalised with shido.
avoid: judoka bent over at the waist to defend

fouls.title: Ippon and safe landing
fouls.text: Ippon is a throw that lands the opponent largely on the back with speed, force and control; the thrower keeps hold of the sleeve so uke can break the fall, and uke tucks the chin and slaps the mat.
fouls.legal: uke's head stays off the mat (chin tucked)
avoid: uke landing on the head or neck
